summary.summary: Chichester is debt-free — no external borrowing and a nil capital financing requirement right across the forecast to 2029/30 — and held £118.757m of investments at 31 March 2026, up £7.2m in the year. Treasury income of £6.030m beat the £4.164m budget, mainly because the council locked in higher-yielding deposits (including £51m with other local authorities) ahead of rate cuts. Its £36.8m of externally managed pooled funds have produced £12.3m of income since purchase in 2016 against a cumulative £3.2m capital loss, which sits behind the IFRS 9 statutory override until April 2029. The £13.13m directly owned commercial property portfolio produced a £640k net surplus, though voids rose to 5.4% from 2.27% a year earlier.

signals.headline: Verified quiet: debt-free (CFR nil, no external borrowing) with £118.757m of investments at 31 March 2026 and treasury income £6.030m against a £4.164m budget
signals.why: A debt-free council with rising cash balances and income well over budget carries minimal treasury credit risk.

news_drafts.headline: Chichester's five-year budget model moves from a £2.3m gap in 2026/27 to a surplus in 2028/29
news_drafts.lead:
Chichester District Council's Cabinet was given a financial plan for 2027/28 to 2031/32 that shows a gap between spending and income of £2.271m in 2026/27, after government funding and council tax. The gap is forecast at £649k in 2027/28. The plan shows a surplus of £231k in 2028/29.

The paper's figures for the later years are surpluses of £1.597m in 2029/30, £2.889m in 2030/31 and £3.488m in 2031/32. The paper shows surpluses in brackets, and it describes the model as high-level. These are forecasts, not outturn (the actual figures once a year has ended).

The paper says the model "is then expected to return to a surplus from 2028-29 onwards, primarily as a result of the new leisure centre management contract". That contract started in May 2026, and the model now reflects its contractual position. The paper says the 2026/27 deficit is driven by rising temporary accommodation costs. The papers given to the desk do not state a separate figure for the leisure contract's effect.
news_drafts.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 2

news_drafts.headline: Chichester's auditor expects a third year without a clean opinion, with 2028/29 the earliest for one
news_drafts.lead:
Chichester District Council's external auditor (an independent check on its accounts) expects to issue a qualified opinion on the 2025/26 accounts, meaning it could not fully sign them off. The draft audit results report went to the Corporate Governance and Audit Committee on 19 October 2026. The 2023/24 accounts received a disclaimed opinion, where the auditor gives no opinion at all, and the 2024/25 accounts a qualified one.

The auditor says gaps remain in its assurance over the value of property, plant and equipment (land, buildings and other long-lived assets), over the council's reserves (money set aside), and over capital grants receipts in advance. The property, plant and equipment balance in the report is £156.449m, of which £137.661m is land and buildings. Investment property is £13.132m. The report says the opinion is subject to remaining procedures being completed.

Assets last revalued in 2022/23 are the issue. The auditor says an unqualified opinion, the full sign-off, is possible by 2028/29 only if they are revalued in 2026/27. The council's stated intention is to revalue them in 2027/28. The auditor's annual report says that timetable puts an unqualified opinion back to 2029/30.
news_drafts.paper_title: CDC Audit Results Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026

findings.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 1
findings.headline: The 2026-27 revenue budget requirement of £18.134m was set 11.0% below the base budget for 2025-26
findings.detail: The paper says the budget was set with a surplus of £145k transferred to reserves. Since then the paper records cost pressures and a decline in planning income for major schemes linked to the economic situation.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare a reported 11.0% year-on-year reduction in the budget requirement against their own budget-setting outcome.
findings.figures: £18.134m revenue budget requirement for 2026-27; 11.0% spending decrease over base budget for 2025-26; £145k surplus transferred to reserves
findings.quote: The Council’s revenue budget requirement for 2026-27 was set at £18.134m, which represented a spending decrease of 11.0% over the base budget for 2025-26.

findings.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 1
findings.headline: All interest receipts can now be applied to revenue, and the paper says in-house investment income has continued to yield significant returns
findings.detail: The paper says that in 2026-27 the key principle for capital receipts and reserves was changed to allow investment interest to fund both capital and revenue. Previously only the more predictable income from long-term multi-asset funds was in the revenue budget. Bank of England Base Rate is 3.75% (September 2026).
findings.matters: A policy change that lets interest income fund revenue is a lever other councils with large cash balances may also be weighing.
findings.figures: Base Rate 3.75% (September 2026); long-term multi-asset funds return around 4% per annum
findings.quote: all interest receipts can legally be applied to revenue expenditure

findings.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 1
findings.headline: The paper says the Government's pause of the LGR programme is likely to delay the implementation timetable for West Sussex reorganisation
findings.detail: The paper says no timeline has been given for the review or its conclusion, so the 2027-28 budget will be developed on a business as usual basis. Committee report templates now include an implications of LGR section, and new capital projects must be considered in terms of timing against the Shadow Authority.
findings.matters: A finance director in a council facing reorganisation can compare how budget and capital timing are being planned around an uncertain transition date.
findings.quote: the recent government announcement to pause the LGR programme whilst it reviews the decisions already taken is likely to delay the implementation timetable

findings.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 1
findings.headline: The 2026-27 pay award of 3.3% exceeded the 3% budget provision, adding some £83k in cost
findings.detail: The paper says the agreed pay award applies across all pay grades. It notes that future pay awards are subject to annual national negotiation and that a higher award than assumed in the model would be a significant risk.
findings.matters: Other councils setting pay budgets against national awards can compare the gap between provision and the agreed award.
findings.figures: 3.3% pay award; 3% provision in 2026-27 budget; cost increase of some £83k; 2027-28 pay assumption of 3.5%
findings.quote: This was higher than the 3% provision made in 2026-27 budget, resulting in a cost increase of some £83k.

findings.paper_title: Financial Strategy and Plan 2027-28 to 2031-32 - Appendix 1
findings.headline: The three-year settlement shows total settlement support falling from £6,968k in 2026-27 to £5,863k in 2028-29
findings.detail: The paper says the settlement consolidated several grants into the unringfenced Revenue Support Grant and created four new ringfenced grants. Revenue Support Grant falls from £4,288k to £3,066k over the period, and retained business rates rise from £2,680k to £2,797k.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare the scale of the fall in settlement support against their own three-year settlement.
findings.figures: Total settlement support £6,968k (2026-27), £6,433k (2027-28), £5,863k (2028-29); Revenue Support Grant £4,288k, £3,692k, £3,066k; total funding £8,119k, £7,621k, £6,916k
findings.quote: The Financial Settlement received in 2026-27 was a three-year settlement spanning the financial years 2026-27 to 2028-29

daily_post.headline: Externally managed pooled funds recorded a capital gain of 0.22% in the first half of 2026-27, while the benchmark average showed a capital loss of 0.12%.
daily_post.lead: Capital movements on pooled funds affect whether a council's investment portfolio gains or loses value, which finance directors and auditors track against budget.
